work these positions to fill gaps between jobs. Temp-to-hire employees can be found in nearly all occupations but are mainly found in multinational corporations (MNCs), especially in the retail and food and beverage (F&B) industries.

Similarly, the F&B industry gravitates towards temp-to-hire employees due to seasonal peaks or last-minute absences. These employees help to keep their businesses running smoothly even with a manpower crunch or increased demands.

Having an agency onboard optimizes the hiring process because your hiring team can offload a lot of the sourcing and screening. You can focus on hiring quality candidates by interviewing those shortlisted by the agency. This also allows you more time for day-to-day operational work and other critical tasks.

Temp-to-hire agencies assume the legal responsibilities of being an employer, from taxes to health insurance coverage and even payroll. They can also help you to avoid unnecessary paperwork. Imagine spending time to enroll these employees for health insurance and other programs and having to terminate the employee or have them quit a few weeks in.
With temp-to-hire employees, you can include them in your systems only when you're confident of the hire. Your hiring team can then focus on only managing the permanent employees.

With the knowledge that they could be converted to a permanent employee, these temp-to-hire employees may be more motivated to prove their capabilities. This could be in the form of contributing more to the team, speaking out, and raising new ideas to earn themselves a permanent place.

Experiencing an especially hectic season? Having additional temp-to-hire employees to lighten the load will be greatly appreciated by the team and will reduce employee burnout. This will create a less-stressed and more confident environment. If temp-to-hire employees prove that they can contribute effectively to the team, they can be offered a chance for conversion.

Furthermore, these employees will also have the chance to build relationships with the permanent employees they’re working with. This saves time in retraining and building new connections as opposed to re-hiring a completely new person for the job should you be using temporary employees.
The cons of temp-to-hire employees

There is a possibility that temp-to-hire employees are less loyal to the company. Since the job is not guaranteed, nor is it always aligned with their passions, these employees might not be as invested as their permanent peers. They may not see the point in building relationships with coworkers or going above and beyond basic responsibilities.
Like every other employee, managing temp-to-hire employees comes with legal risks. With laws on worker statuses and eligibility, contracts have to be well drafted. Some

Temp-to-hire workers should also still be treated with respect and without discrimination to prevent lawsuits. You should always investigate an agency’s treatment of employees before signing on to work with them.

The agency is unlikely to have a full understanding of your company's culture. This means that shortlisted applicants may possess the right skills and experiences, but may not be the right fit for the rest of your team in other aspects. The good news is that this can be resolved easily, by implementing an internal screening process in addition to the agency's recruitment procedure.

The US economy and labor market from 2025 to 2026 are at a historic turning point. From a macroeconomic perspective, the US economy showed a certain resilience in 2025, with real GDP growth hovering around 2.0%. However, labor market trends present a picture that contrasts with these solid macro indicators.
Net job growth throughout 2025 was only 116,000, the slowest pace of employment growth since 2003, excluding recessionary periods.

This stagnation in employment was extremely skewed toward specific sectors; while the healthcare and social assistance sector created approximately 686,100 jobs annually, the rest of the industry groups effectively lost over 500,000 jobs, marking a severe polarization.

Labor market uncertainty has continued into 2026. According to data from the second quarter of 2026, although there was a rebound in employment in March, the number of new jobs added in June was only 57,000, confirming a slowdown in hiring activity once again. Bosch Rexroth Joins Initiative to Support Digitalization of German Mid-Sized Companies, Invests in "Next Level Mittelstand"

German industrial equipment giant Bosch Rexroth has joined the "Next Level Mittelstand" initiative as a new shareholder, aiming to promote the digitalization of mid-sized companies (Mittelstand) in Germany.
Next Level Mittelstand
The six shareholders, including the company, and 23 participating firms will jointly work on standardizing digital adoption procedures and developing implementation guidelines.

This initiative was established in April 2024 with the goal of strengthening the competitiveness of small and medium-sized manufacturing enterprises. It networks major technology companies, startups, IT firms, and manufacturers to support the sharing of practical knowledge and the construction of future digitalization strategies.

According to the German Economic Institute, more than 99% of companies in the country are small and medium-sized enterprises, accounting for approximately 70% of employees. Thomas Fechner, a member of the Bosch Rexroth board of management responsible for the Factory Automation business, stated the following regarding the importance of digitalization:

"Digitalization is a massive opportunity for mid-sized companies to increase their competitiveness in the future. 'Next Level Mittelstand' will be an ideal platform to unlock that potential across the entire industry."
